statement_record.book: Let V = (V, ≤, I, ⊗) be a symmetric monoidal preorder with all joins. Then V is closed (has ⊸, hence is a quantale) if and only if ⊗ distributes over joins: v ⊗ ⋁A = ⋁_{a∈A}(v ⊗ a) for every v and every subset A. Forward by Prop 2.87(b); conversely distributivity makes − ⊗ v join-preserving, so the Chapter-1 adjoint functor theorem for preorders gives a right adjoint, explicitly v ⊸ w := ⋁{a : a ⊗ v ≤ w}.
statement_record.intree: prod_coprod_r : x × (y + z) ≅ x × y + x × z and prod_zero_r : x × 0 ≅ 0, both proved under `{@Cartesian C} `{@Cocartesian C} `{@Closed C _}` and packaged as BiCCC_Distributive : @Distributive C _ _ _; left_adjoint_preserves_colimits (A : F ⊣ U) : PreservesAllColimits F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the FORWARD implication, and only in a restricted form. (i) One direction: nothing in the tree derives closedness from distributivity — the converse needs an adjoint functor theorem, and the in-tree AFT (Adjunction/GAFT.v:241 GAFT) carries strictly more hypotheses than the preorder case needs (a Complete C, PreservesImageLimit and a SolutionSet at every object) and is stated only in the 'limit-preserving U ⇒ U has a LEFT adjoint' direction, never dualized to 'colimit-preserving ⇒ has a right adjoint' and never applied to − ⊗ v. (ii) Finite only: distributivity is proved for binary coproducts and the initial object, not for arbitrary joins ⋁A. (iii) Cartesian tensor only: prod_coprod_r lives over @Cartesian + @Closed, and the general closed-monoidal class Structure/Monoidal/Closed.v:46 ClosedMonoidal itself bundles closed_is_cartesian : @CartesianMonoidal C, so even the general closed base is cartesian; the genuinely general base Structure/Monoidal/StarAutonomous.v:109 SymMonClosed carries no colimit or distributivity statement. (iv) No quantale: there is no join-complete monoidal preorder in the tree, so the biconditional cannot be stated, and the explicit residuation formula v ⊸ w := ⋁{a : a ⊗ v ≤ w} appears nowhere.
